title: One image. A career of possibilities.
thesis: BLTZ connects approved imagery to an athlete’s permanent career identity, helping fans and producers discover a specific use and request the right license.

uses.title: Print on demand
uses.buyer: Fan, through a Getty-approved print partner
uses.example: A career-defining photograph offered as a physical print from the player’s Locker.
uses.revenue: Getty receives the agreed license fee or sales-based payment. Player participation and fulfillment costs require separate agreed terms.
uses.approval: Approve Locker display and print resale separately; confirm third-party rights, seller, pricing and fulfillment.
uses.track: Asset ID → Locker referral → print order → Getty payment; creator credit and any contracted player payout.

uses.title: Player podcast
uses.buyer: Player’s media business or podcast producer
uses.example: A player and former teammate discuss a career moment with its licensed still shown on screen.
uses.revenue: Getty receives a license fee quoted for the episode and approved channels. Podcast income is separate from image licensing.
uses.approval: Specify episode, channels, audience, territory and term; quote promotional clips or social use separately if needed.
uses.track: Asset ID → episode license → published URL + credit → episode views and Getty license revenue.

uses.title: Player documentary
uses.example: A production team discovers an athlete’s history through the Locker and requests a still for a documentary scene.
uses.revenue: Getty receives a license fee based on the production’s intended use. Additional uses may require additional licensing.
uses.approval: Submit production title, scene/use, distribution, territory and term; agree clearance and credit requirements.
uses.track: Asset ID → production inquiry → license → scene + credit record → Getty license revenue.

pilot.title: Proposed 50-player pilot
pilot.scope: 50 opt-in players · Up to 3 approved stills each · Maximum 150 unique images
pilot.stages: Validate player demand → Agree approved uses + pricing → Clear imagery → Launch + measure → Joint review
pilot.boundary: Begin with approved Locker display and selected use cases; expand only after clearance. Duration, budget and success targets to agree with Getty.
pilot.getty: Getty: define eligible imagery, quote each use, approve rights/credit requirements and provide a licensing contact.
pilot.bltz: BLTZ: recruit players, gather use briefs, link imagery to career moments, route requests and report attributable activity.

metrics.label: Demand
metrics.value: Player interviews, selected images and qualified license requests

metrics.label: Exposure
metrics.value: Locker views, episode/social views and tracked referrals where available

metrics.label: Revenue
metrics.value: Paid licenses or print orders, Getty receipts and repeat buyer requests

note: Discussion proposal, not an existing Getty agreement. Each use needs appropriate approval and a use-specific quote. Views are engagement, not license revenue. Creator attribution does not itself create payment entitlement; royalties, referral fees and player shares apply only if contracted.
workflowTitle: From discovery to a paid, credited use.

workflowSteps.title: Connect
workflowSteps.body: Retain Getty asset ID, source and creator credit; connect the image to the athlete and career moment.

workflowSteps.title: Specify
workflowSteps.body: Identify buyer, intended use, channel, territory and term. Locker display permission is separate from downstream use.

workflowSteps.title: Approve + license
workflowSteps.body: Getty quotes the use; required rights and approvals are confirmed before publication, resale or production use.

workflowSteps.title: Attribute + measure
workflowSteps.body: Record license, use location, credit, referral and payment reference. Pay participants only under agreed contracts.
